title: Root Canal Treatment in Malviya Nagar
body:
[gd_img name="dr-shikha-reception" alt="Dr Shikha Goel, endodontist, at the Goel Dental reception" cap="Dr Shikha Goel, endodontist"]

Signs you may need one

  • Pain that wakes you, or lingering pain after hot or cold
  • Swelling or pus near the tooth or gum
  • A deep cavity, crack or injury reaching the nerve
  • A darkened or loose tooth
  • An earlier root canal that has failed

Only an exam and X-ray confirm it. Some teeth need just a filling; a few cannot be saved.

What happens, step by step

  1. Exam and digital X-ray (RVG) to confirm the diagnosis.
  2. Local anaesthetic so the area is numb.
  3. Cleaning the canals with rotary files; length measured with an apex locator; rubber dam to keep saliva out.
  4. Sealing with gutta-percha, using warm obturation (System B).
  5. A crown on most back teeth so the tooth does not break when chewing.

One visit or several?

Most root canals take one to three visits. Some teeth can be finished in one sitting: see single-sitting root canal. Molars, re-treatments and cracked teeth may need the dental microscope.

The clinic makes zirconia and ceramic crowns on site (CAD/CAM), so the crown can sometimes be fitted the same day.

Root canal or extraction?

If a tooth can be saved, a root canal with a crown keeps your natural tooth and bite. An extracted tooth usually needs an implant or bridge; otherwise nearby teeth can drift.

After treatment

Mild soreness for a few days is common, more often after a repeat root canal. Ordinary pain relief usually helps and it settles within about a week. Call if you have swelling, fever or pain that is getting worse.

Questions patients ask

How much does a root canal cost at Goel Dental?

A root canal costs ₹4,500 for a front tooth, ₹5,500 for a premolar and ₹6,500 for a molar. Single-sitting is ₹7,500 and microscopic ₹8,500. Back teeth usually also need a crown, from ₹6,500. Your exact fee is given in writing after the exam.

Does a root canal hurt?

The tooth is numbed with local anaesthetic first, so most patients feel pressure rather than pain. Mild soreness for a few days afterwards is common and settles with ordinary pain relief. Laughing-gas sedation is available for anxious patients.

How many visits does a root canal take?

Most root canals take one to three visits of 15–30 minutes. Some teeth, with little infection and no swelling, can be finished in one 30–60 minute sitting. The endodontist decides after the X-ray.

Do I need a crown after a root canal?

Usually yes for back teeth. A root-canal-treated molar or premolar can crack when chewing without a crown. Front teeth sometimes need only a filling. Goel Dental can make zirconia or ceramic crowns on site, often the same day.

Is a root canal better than pulling the tooth?

If the tooth can be saved, a root canal with a crown keeps your natural tooth and bite. An extracted tooth usually needs an implant or bridge, otherwise nearby teeth can drift into the gap.

Who does root canals at Goel Dental?

Dr Shikha Goel, an endodontist (MDS in Conservative Dentistry and Endodontics), does the root canals, with a dental microscope available for molars, re-treatments and cracked teeth.

title: Single-Sitting Root Canal Treatment
body:
Who it suits

  • Teeth being prepared for a crown or veneer for cosmetic reasons
  • Sensitivity with little or no pain
  • No pus or swelling, and no infection visible on the X-ray
  • Teeth that have not had a root canal before

No equipment makes one-visit treatment right for every tooth. Dr Goel decides after the X-ray. If the tooth is not suitable, the standard root canal is done over two or three visits.

How it is done in one visit

Digital X-ray (RVG), CBCT for complex roots, rubber dam isolation, rotary NiTi files (X-Smart), an apex locator, a dental microscope when needed, and warm obturation to seal the canals.

Is it more painful?

No more than a multi-visit root canal. Any soreness afterwards is usually mild and settles with ordinary pain relief.

Crown the same day

With the on-site CAD/CAM system, a zirconia or ceramic crown can often be made and fitted the same day. See crowns and bridges.

Fee

Single-sitting root canal: ₹7,500. Crown extra.

Questions patients ask

How long does a single-sitting root canal take?

Usually 30–60 minutes from start to finish, in one appointment.

Can every tooth have a single-sitting root canal?

No. It suits teeth with little or no infection. Teeth with pus, swelling, severe pain or a failed earlier root canal usually need more than one visit so the infection can settle first.

How much does a single-sitting root canal cost?

₹7,500 on the clinic's 2026 fee list, plus a crown if the tooth needs one.

Can I get the crown on the same day?

Often yes. Goel Dental designs and mills zirconia or ceramic crowns on site with a CAD/CAM system, so the root canal and crown can sometimes be completed in one visit.

title: Microscopic Root Canal Treatment
body:
[gd_img name="micro-rct" alt="Ceiling-mounted dental operating microscope at Goel Dental" cap="Labomed ceiling-mounted dental microscope"]

When the microscope helps

  • Finding extra fine canals in molars (such as MB2)
  • Seeing micro-cracks in the tooth
  • Retrieving a broken instrument
  • Re-treating a failed root canal
  • Keeping more natural tooth structure

Equipment used

A Labomed ceiling-mounted microscope with up to 25× magnification and a 50,000-lux light, plus rubber dam, a Root ZX mini apex locator, ultrasonic irrigation, EndoVac negative-pressure irrigation and System B warm obturation.

Fee

Microscopic root canal: ₹8,500. [gd_confirm]Clinic to confirm fee[/gd_confirm]

Most teeth do not need the microscope; see standard root canal treatment.

Questions patients ask

What is a microscopic root canal?

A root canal done under a dental microscope with up to 25× magnification. It helps find very fine extra canals, see cracks and retrieve broken instruments, so it is used for molars, re-treatments and difficult teeth.

When do I need a microscopic root canal?

When a molar has hard-to-find canals, a previous root canal has failed, a tooth may be cracked, or an instrument has broken inside a canal. Most routine root canals do not need the microscope.

How much does a microscopic root canal cost?

₹8,500 on the clinic's 2026 fee list, compared with ₹4,500–6,500 for a standard root canal.

title: Dental Emergency in Malviya Nagar
body:
Go to a hospital emergency department now if swelling spreads to the eye or neck, or you have fever, trouble breathing or trouble swallowing.

Call or WhatsApp first

Phone [gd_phone] or [gd_wa t="Emergency"] with a photo. Same-day emergency appointments: [gd_confirm]Clinic to confirm same-day policy and after-hours number[/gd_confirm]

First aid while you travel

Severe toothache

Rinse with warm salt water, floss gently to remove trapped food, and take ordinary pain relief as directed on the pack. Do not put aspirin on the gum.

Broken or chipped tooth

Rinse with warm water, keep any piece in milk, hold a cold compress on the cheek and avoid chewing on that side.

Knocked-out adult tooth

Hold it by the crown, not the root. Rinse briefly in milk. Put it back in the socket if you can, or keep it in milk, and come in straight away. The first hour matters most.

Bleeding after an extraction

Bite firmly on folded gauze for 30 minutes without checking. Sit upright; avoid rinsing and hot drinks. Call if it does not settle.

Swollen gum or face

Hold a cold compress on the outside of the cheek and call the clinic. Do not apply heat.

What usually happens at the visit

An exam and X-ray, then relief of pain: often starting a root canal, an extraction, or bonding a chipped tooth. Consultation ₹500; X-ray ₹150 for 1–3 teeth. [gd_confirm]Clinic to confirm[/gd_confirm]

Questions patients ask

What counts as a dental emergency?

Severe toothache, swelling of the gum or face, a broken or knocked-out tooth, and bleeding that will not stop after an extraction. Call the clinic before you travel so the dentist can fit you in.

When should I go to a hospital instead of a dentist?

Go to a hospital emergency department straight away if swelling spreads towards the eye or neck, or if you have fever, difficulty breathing or difficulty swallowing.

What should I do if a tooth is knocked out?

Hold it by the crown, not the root. Rinse briefly in milk, put it back in the socket if you can or keep it in milk, and get to a dentist immediately. The first hour matters most.

How do I stop a toothache until I see the dentist?

Rinse with warm salt water, floss gently to remove trapped food and take ordinary pain relief as directed on the pack. Do not put aspirin on the gum. A toothache usually needs treatment, so book an exam.

How much is an emergency visit?

A consultation is ₹500 and an X-ray of 1–3 teeth ₹150 on the 2026 fee list. Treatment fees, such as starting a root canal or an extraction, are explained before anything is done.

title: Dental Implants in Malviya Nagar
body:
[gd_img name="implant-model" alt="Dental implant model showing implant, abutment and crown" cap="Implant, abutment and crown"]

Who it is for

  • One missing tooth, without cutting down the teeth beside it
  • Several missing teeth: individual implants or an implant bridge
  • All teeth in a jaw: see All-on-4 and All-on-6
  • Loose dentures that need support

Bone, gum health and medical history decide suitability. Bone grafting or a sinus lift may be needed first.

How treatment runs

  1. Free consultation and CBCT scan to measure the bone and plan the position.
  2. Placement under local anaesthetic, guided by a digital plan and 3D-printed guide where suitable.
  3. Healing, usually a few months, while the implant bonds with the bone.
  4. Crown fitted on the implant.

Fees by implant system

If a missing tooth is not replaced

Neighbouring teeth can drift into the gap, the jaw bone there slowly shrinks, and chewing shifts to other teeth.

Implant, bridge or denture?

A bridge is faster but needs the teeth either side cut down. A denture costs least but is removable. An implant stands alone and preserves bone. The dentist explains which suits you after the scan.

Questions patients ask

How much does a dental implant cost at Goel Dental?

From ₹17,000 per implant (Adin or Alpha Bio) to ₹55,000 (Straumann), with Osstem at ₹35,000 and Nobel Biocare at ₹40,000–45,000. The crown on top is extra, ₹8,500–17,000. The consultation is free.

Is the implant consultation free?

Yes, according to the clinic's 2026 fee list. A CBCT 3D scan, if needed for planning, costs ₹2,500–4,500.

How long does the implant process take?

Usually a few months: the implant is placed, heals into the bone, and then the crown is fitted. It takes longer if bone grafting or a sinus lift is needed first.

Am I suitable for a dental implant?

Most adults with enough healthy jaw bone and gums are suitable. Smoking, uncontrolled diabetes and bone loss can affect healing. A CBCT scan and medical history decide suitability.

Implant or bridge: which is better?

An implant stands on its own and keeps the jaw bone in place. A bridge is quicker but needs the teeth either side cut down for crowns. The dentist explains which suits you after the scan.

Do you offer EMI for implants?

Yes, on leading credit cards. Ask the front desk which cards and tenures apply.

title: Full-Mouth Dental Implants: All-on-4 and All-on-6
body:
All-on-4

Four implants placed at planned angles support a complete set of fixed teeth. Angling the back implants uses the bone that is available, which often avoids extensive grafting.

All-on-6

Six implants spread the biting load further and add stability, which can help when bone density is lower or extra support is needed.

How it is planned

A CBCT 3D scan, digital planning and a 3D-printed surgical guide place each implant in the planned position. The clinic has OPG and CBCT on site.

Who it suits

  • Most or all teeth missing in a jaw
  • Loose or uncomfortable dentures
  • Teeth that cannot be saved across a whole arch

Fee

Questions patients ask

What is All-on-4?

A fixed set of teeth for a whole jaw held by four implants. The back implants are angled to use the bone that is available, which often avoids extensive bone grafting.

What is the difference between All-on-4 and All-on-6?

All-on-6 uses six implants instead of four, spreading the biting load further for extra stability. It can help when bone density is lower.

How much does All-on-4 cost?

₹90,000–1,00,000 per arch on the clinic's 2026 fee list.

Are All-on-4 teeth fixed or removable?

Fixed. They are screwed onto the implants and removed only by the dentist for maintenance.

When you may need a crown

  • After a root canal on a back tooth
  • A broken, cracked or heavily filled tooth
  • Severe wear or sensitivity
  • Short, discoloured or misshapen teeth
  • On top of a dental implant

Bridges

A bridge is at least three crowns joined together to replace one or more missing teeth, anchored on the teeth either side. With good hygiene, bridges can last 10–15 years.

How long does a dental bridge last?

With good brushing, flossing and regular check-ups, bridges commonly last 10–15 years.

title: Wisdom Tooth Extraction in Malviya Nagar
body:
[gd_img name="opg" alt="OPG full-mouth X-ray machine at Goel Dental" cap="On-site OPG for wisdom tooth assessment"]

Does it need to come out?

The clinic's rule: if a wisdom tooth is not causing pain and shows no problem on the X-ray, it can stay. Removal is advised for:

  • Repeated pain or swelling around the tooth
  • Deep decay that is hard to clean
  • Damage to the tooth in front of it
  • A cyst forming around it

How it is done

  1. X-ray and OPG on site to see the tooth's position; CBCT for complex cases.
  2. Local anaesthetic; minimally invasive technique by the oral surgeon.
  3. PRP may be applied to help healing.
  4. Aftercare instructions and a review.

Recovery

Facial swelling can occur, more often after lower wisdom teeth. Cold compresses straight after help. Two wisdom teeth on the same side can usually be removed in one sitting.

Fee

Wisdom tooth extraction from ₹2,500. [gd_confirm]Clinic to confirm fee range[/gd_confirm]

Questions patients ask

Does every wisdom tooth need to be removed?

No. If a wisdom tooth causes no pain and shows no problem on the X-ray, it can stay. Removal is advised for repeated pain or swelling, deep decay, damage to the next tooth, or a cyst.

How much does wisdom tooth removal cost?

From ₹2,500 per tooth. The fee depends on how the tooth is positioned, which the on-site OPG X-ray shows.

How long is recovery after wisdom tooth removal?

Most people return to normal routine the next day. Swelling can last a few days, especially after lower wisdom teeth; cold compresses straight after the extraction help.

Can wisdom teeth removal affect eyesight?

No. This is a myth. Wisdom teeth are not connected to the eyes.

Who removes wisdom teeth at Goel Dental?

The clinic's in-house oral and maxillofacial surgeon (MDS) handles wisdom teeth and complex extractions.

title: Tooth Extraction in Malviya Nagar
body:
When a tooth is extracted

  • Decay or a crack too large to repair
  • Advanced gum disease with a very loose tooth
  • Milk teeth that have not fallen out on time
  • Creating space for braces

If the tooth can be saved, a root canal is usually the better choice.

Aftercare

  • Bite on gauze for 30 minutes
  • No rinsing, spitting or hot drinks for 24 hours
  • Soft, cool food the first day
  • Call if bleeding does not settle

Replacing the tooth

Options are an implant, a bridge or a denture.

Fee

Simple extraction: ₹500–2,500 per tooth, from the clinic's published price page. [gd_confirm]Clinic to confirm[/gd_confirm]

Questions patients ask

How much does a tooth extraction cost?

A simple extraction is ₹500–2,500 per tooth on the clinic's published price list. Wisdom teeth start from ₹2,500.

Does tooth extraction hurt?

The area is numbed with local anaesthetic, so you feel pressure but not sharp pain. Mild soreness afterwards usually settles in a few days.

What should I avoid after an extraction?

For 24 hours avoid rinsing, spitting, smoking, straws and hot drinks. Bite on gauze for 30 minutes and eat soft, cool food the first day.

Should I replace an extracted tooth?

Usually yes, to stop nearby teeth drifting. Options are an implant, a bridge or a denture.

title: Teeth Cleaning (Scaling and Polishing) in Malviya Nagar
body:
[gd_img name="cleaning" alt="Teeth cleaning at Goel Dental" cap="Scaling and polishing"]

Why cleaning matters

Tartar holds bacteria against the gums. Left alone it leads to bleeding gums, bad breath and, over time, gum disease and loose teeth.

Two ways to clean

MethodBest for
Ultrasonic scaling and polishingRoutine tartar and stains
EMS GBT airflowSensitive teeth, braces, crowns, veneers and implants

How often

Every six months suits most people; more often with gum disease, braces or implants.

Fee

Scaling and polishing: ₹2,500 on the 2026 fee list. [gd_confirm]Clinic to confirm[/gd_confirm]

Questions patients ask

How much does teeth cleaning cost?

Scaling and polishing is ₹2,500 on the clinic's 2026 fee list.

How often should I get my teeth cleaned?

Every six months suits most people. People with gum disease, braces or implants may need cleaning more often.

Does scaling damage enamel?

No. Scaling removes hardened tartar, not enamel. Teeth can feel sensitive for a few days afterwards.

Will cleaning make my teeth whiter?

It removes surface stains, so teeth often look brighter. A lighter shade than your natural colour needs whitening, which is a separate treatment.

title: EMS GBT (Guided Biofilm Therapy) Teeth Cleaning
body:
How it works

  1. Biofilm detection: a disclosing stain shows where plaque is.
  2. Airflow with warm water and 14 µm erythritol granules removes plaque and stains.
  3. Soft tissue cleaning of gums, cheeks and tongue.
  4. Tartar remaining is removed with a fine scaler tip.

Who benefits

  • People with very sensitive teeth
  • Braces wearers
  • Crowns, veneers and implants
  • Children, who often find it easier than scaling

Results

Real cases are shown on the homepage before/after sliders. [gd_confirm]Confirm patient consent[/gd_confirm]

Fee

[gd_confirm]Fee needed for EMS GBT[/gd_confirm] Standard scaling and polishing is ₹2,500.

Questions patients ask

What is EMS GBT cleaning?

Guided Biofilm Therapy: plaque is stained so it can be seen, then removed with a fine airflow of warm water and erythritol powder. Any remaining tartar is removed with a fine scaler tip.

Is EMS GBT better for sensitive teeth?

It uses warm water and a gentle airflow, which many people with sensitive teeth find more comfortable than standard scaling.

Can I have EMS GBT with braces or implants?

Yes. It is suited to braces, crowns, veneers and implants, where routine scaling is harder.

title: Gum Disease Treatment and Bleeding Gums
body:
Signs of gum disease

  • Bleeding when brushing or flossing
  • Red, swollen or tender gums
  • Bad breath that does not go away
  • Gums pulling back from the teeth
  • Loose or shifting teeth

How it is treated

  1. Gum assessment with pocket measurements and X-rays.
  2. Professional cleaning: scaling or EMS GBT.
  3. Deep cleaning below the gumline where pockets are deep.
  4. Laser gum treatment with a BIOLASE soft-tissue laser where needed.
  5. Maintenance visits every 3–6 months.

Your periodontist

Dr Ambica Sharma, MDS (Periodontics), Govt Dental College Ahmedabad; three years as Senior Resident at AIIMS. [gd_confirm]Confirm she is on the current team[/gd_confirm]

Fees

[gd_confirm]Fees needed for deep cleaning and laser gum treatment[/gd_confirm]

Questions patients ask

Why do my gums bleed when I brush?

Bleeding when brushing is the most common early sign of gum disease (gingivitis), caused by plaque and tartar at the gumline. A professional cleaning and better brushing and flossing usually reverse it.

Is gum disease curable?

Early gum disease is reversible with cleaning and good home care. Advanced gum disease can be controlled with deep cleaning, laser treatment and regular maintenance, but lost bone does not grow back on its own.

What does a periodontist do?

A periodontist is a gum specialist. At Goel Dental, Dr Ambica Sharma assesses gum pockets, plans deep cleaning and laser gum treatment, and manages maintenance.

Can loose teeth be saved?

Sometimes, if gum disease is treated early. The periodontist measures the pockets and X-rays the bone to decide.

title: Clear Aligners (Invisible Braces) in Malviya Nagar
body:

Why people choose aligners

  • Hard to notice when worn
  • Removed for eating, drinking, brushing and flossing
  • No brackets or wires

Who they suit

Crowded or widely spaced teeth and many bite problems in adults and teens. Severe cases may still need fixed braces. The orthodontist decides after a scan.

How treatment runs

  1. Exam, photos and scan
  2. Planned tooth movement, often with a preview of the result
  3. A new set of aligners about every two weeks
  4. Review visits about monthly; usually 18–30 aligners over about a year

Brands and fees

The current site names Clearpath; Invisalign cases appear on the cosmetic site. [gd_confirm]Which aligner brands, and fees for each[/gd_confirm]

Questions patients ask

How long does clear aligner treatment take?

A typical case takes about a year, using 18–30 aligners changed about every two weeks, with check-ups about monthly.

Are clear aligners as effective as braces?

For most crowding and spacing, yes. Severe bite problems may still need fixed braces. The orthodontist decides after a scan.

Can I eat with aligners in?

No. Take them out to eat and to drink anything other than water, then brush before putting them back.

How many hours a day should I wear aligners?

Most of the day and night, removing them only to eat, drink and clean your teeth. Your orthodontist confirms the hours for your plan.

title: Children's Dentistry in Malviya Nagar
body:
[gd_img name="kids" alt="Child at a dental check-up at Goel Dental" cap="Children's room"]

Why milk teeth matter

An infected milk tooth can damage the permanent tooth growing beneath it, and losing milk teeth early can cause crowding later.

Preventive care

  • Fluoride application every 4–6 months; a 2-minute procedure
  • Pit and fissure sealants to protect back teeth
  • Routine check-ups to catch cavities, habits (thumb sucking, tongue thrusting) and bite problems early

Treatment

  • Kids' fillings and root canals
  • Early orthodontic checks
  • Laughing-gas sedation for anxious children

Fees

[gd_confirm]Fees needed for children's treatments[/gd_confirm]

Questions patients ask

When should my child first see a dentist?

When the first tooth appears, or by the first birthday at the latest.

Do milk teeth need fillings if they will fall out?

Yes. An infected milk tooth can harm the adult tooth forming beneath it, and losing milk teeth early can cause crowding later.

How often should children have fluoride application?

Every 4–6 months. It takes about two minutes and strengthens enamel against cavities.

What if my child is scared of the dentist?

Children are seen in a separate children's room, and laughing-gas sedation is available for anxious children.

Pain & emergencies

What counts as a dental emergency?

Severe toothache, swelling of the gum or face, a broken or knocked-out tooth, and bleeding that will not stop after an extraction. Call the clinic before you travel so the dentist can fit you in. Dental emergency →

When should I go to a hospital instead of a dentist?

Go to a hospital emergency department straight away if swelling spreads towards the eye or neck, or if you have fever, difficulty breathing or difficulty swallowing. Dental emergency →

What should I do if a tooth is knocked out?

Hold it by the crown, not the root. Rinse briefly in milk, put it back in the socket if you can or keep it in milk, and get to a dentist immediately. The first hour matters most. Dental emergency →

How much does a root canal cost at Goel Dental?

A root canal costs ₹4,500 for a front tooth, ₹5,500 for a premolar and ₹6,500 for a molar. Single-sitting is ₹7,500 and microscopic ₹8,500. Back teeth usually also need a crown, from ₹6,500. Your exact fee is given in writing after the exam. Root canal treatment →

Does a root canal hurt?

The tooth is numbed with local anaesthetic first, so most patients feel pressure rather than pain. Mild soreness for a few days afterwards is common and settles with ordinary pain relief. Laughing-gas sedation is available for anxious patients. Root canal treatment →

How many visits does a root canal take?

Most root canals take one to three visits of 15–30 minutes. Some teeth, with little infection and no swelling, can be finished in one 30–60 minute sitting. The endodontist decides after the X-ray. Root canal treatment →

How long does a single-sitting root canal take?

Usually 30–60 minutes from start to finish, in one appointment. Single-sitting root canal →

Can every tooth have a single-sitting root canal?

No. It suits teeth with little or no infection. Teeth with pus, swelling, severe pain or a failed earlier root canal usually need more than one visit so the infection can settle first. Single-sitting root canal →

How much does a single-sitting root canal cost?

₹7,500 on the clinic's 2026 fee list, plus a crown if the tooth needs one. Single-sitting root canal →

What is a microscopic root canal?

A root canal done under a dental microscope with up to 25× magnification. It helps find very fine extra canals, see cracks and retrieve broken instruments, so it is used for molars, re-treatments and difficult teeth. Microscopic root canal →

When do I need a microscopic root canal?

When a molar has hard-to-find canals, a previous root canal has failed, a tooth may be cracked, or an instrument has broken inside a canal. Most routine root canals do not need the microscope. Microscopic root canal →

How much does a microscopic root canal cost?

₹8,500 on the clinic's 2026 fee list, compared with ₹4,500–6,500 for a standard root canal. Microscopic root canal →

Implants & crowns

How much does a dental implant cost at Goel Dental?

From ₹17,000 per implant (Adin or Alpha Bio) to ₹55,000 (Straumann), with Osstem at ₹35,000 and Nobel Biocare at ₹40,000–45,000. The crown on top is extra, ₹8,500–17,000. The consultation is free. Dental implants →

Is the implant consultation free?

Yes, according to the clinic's 2026 fee list. A CBCT 3D scan, if needed for planning, costs ₹2,500–4,500. Dental implants →

How long does the implant process take?

Usually a few months: the implant is placed, heals into the bone, and then the crown is fitted. It takes longer if bone grafting or a sinus lift is needed first. Dental implants →

What is All-on-4?

A fixed set of teeth for a whole jaw held by four implants. The back implants are angled to use the bone that is available, which often avoids extensive bone grafting. All-on-4 / All-on-6 implants →

What is the difference between All-on-4 and All-on-6?

All-on-6 uses six implants instead of four, spreading the biting load further for extra stability. It can help when bone density is lower. All-on-4 / All-on-6 implants →

How much does All-on-4 cost?

₹90,000–1,00,000 per arch on the clinic's 2026 fee list. All-on-4 / All-on-6 implants →

Can I get a crown in one day?

Often yes. The tooth is scanned, and the crown is designed and milled on site with a Dentsply Sirona CAD/CAM system, then fitted in the same appointment. Crowns & bridges →

Which crown is best after a root canal?

Metal-free zirconia or ceramic crowns look most natural and are strong; metal-ceramic crowns are a lower-cost choice for back teeth. Ask to see samples before deciding. Crowns & bridges →

Does every wisdom tooth need to be removed?

No. If a wisdom tooth causes no pain and shows no problem on the X-ray, it can stay. Removal is advised for repeated pain or swelling, deep decay, damage to the next tooth, or a cyst. Wisdom tooth extraction →

From ₹2,500 per tooth. The fee depends on how the tooth is positioned, which the on-site OPG X-ray shows. Wisdom tooth extraction →

How long is recovery after wisdom tooth removal?

Most people return to normal routine the next day. Swelling can last a few days, especially after lower wisdom teeth; cold compresses straight after the extraction help. Wisdom tooth extraction →

A simple extraction is ₹500–2,500 per tooth on the clinic's published price list. Wisdom teeth start from ₹2,500. Tooth extraction →

Does tooth extraction hurt?

The area is numbed with local anaesthetic, so you feel pressure but not sharp pain. Mild soreness afterwards usually settles in a few days. Tooth extraction →

What should I avoid after an extraction?

For 24 hours avoid rinsing, spitting, smoking, straws and hot drinks. Bite on gauze for 30 minutes and eat soft, cool food the first day. Tooth extraction →

Every six months suits most people. People with gum disease, braces or implants may need cleaning more often. Teeth cleaning →
